body: Code for the paper Hybrid Spectrogram and Waveform Source Separation
plain_description: Demucs separates any song into its individual components — drums, bass, vocals, and other instruments — with state-of-the-art accuracy. Musicians and producers can isolate stems for remixing, karaoke, or audio cleanup without needing a studio. The big picture: it's a free, open-source tool that delivers professional-grade source separation on a standard computer.
technical_description: Demucs is a music source separation library implementing Hybrid Transformer Demucs (v4), a U-Net convolutional architecture with cross-domain Transformer encoders operating on both spectrogram and waveform representations. It provides a CLI tool and Python API for separating audio into drums, bass, vocals, and accompaniment stems. The model supports GPU acceleration (minimum 3 GB VRAM) and CPU fallback, with processing time roughly 1.5x track duration on CPU. Pre-trained models include htdemucs, htdemucs_ft, htdemucs_6s, hdemucs_mmi, and MDX variants. Installation is via pip, with optional conda environments for training. The project is released under the MIT license and is no longer actively maintained.
title: Demucs Music Source Separation
